note: Talent is the depth-weighted recruiting composite, enriched with published transfer-portal valuations. It is what the rating uses. Production is the same teams scored from play-by-play and is NOT in any rating: swapping it into the composite moved prediction by -0.0119 points of mean absolute error, 95% CI [-0.037, +0.013] -- indistinguishable from zero. Production is a T-SCORE: 50 is the league average and 10 is one standard deviation. It covers the OFFENSIVE SKILL POSITIONS ONLY -- QB, RB, WR, TE and P -- because those are the players a play-by-play names, so it says nothing about a line or a defence; the Measured column shows how many players it rests on, and a team below three is not ranked at all. Adding the defensive rooms was tested and rejected: on the same teams it cut split-half reliability from 0.665 to 0.612 and year-over-year persistence from 0.594 to 0.554. The two columns are shown as RANKS because their scales are not comparable: talent spreads over a standard deviation of 21 composite points and production is shrunk toward the league by coverage before it is standardised. Subtracting them would make every strong roster look like it underachieves and every thin one like it overachieves, by construction.
